pr_body:
Use EPERM not "1" in errtest.
Add comments on error code format, update documentation.
Clean up some code in err library.

This started because I gave an obscure comment https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/12276#issuecomment-650166747 and I was challenged to make a PR.  So here it is.  I think this fixes #12217, but it does it by fully removing
the function name (which we removed internally anyway).
pr_comments: This also uses the symbolic name EPERM instead of "1" and skips the test if the value of EPERM is too big.
I don't think function strings should remain.  We don't use them, and we don't have much evidence that people do anything with OpenSSL's error code stuff in their own code.

> I don't think function strings should remain. We don't use them,

Er, we don't? So if the error output shows you a function name, that's not useful? I wholeheartedly disagree.
We added this so we wouldn't have to keep using `_F_` macros and their associated strings, and switched to use `_func_` and similar instead. Have you forgotten?

>>We don't use function names

>Er, we don't?

No, we don't.   We made a conscious decision to stop putting internal OpenSSL fuction names.  The func-name stuff isn't used by openssl, and won't be because of that decision.  It *might possibly* by useful, but there are other ways -- error-data -- to get the same thing.

@richsalz, look back at #9452.  That's the main PR that *replaced* the old function indicators (`_F_` macros with associated strings) with the new (based on `OPENSSL_FUNC`).  We didn't decide to remove function indicators altogether, we only decided that we want to get rid of the old.

Now, for some reason, *you* want to get rid of function indicators altogether...  but that doesn't mean that *"we"* want that.

I'll see your #9452, and raise you #9441 :)

> This is what you want .. not what *we* want.

Aren't many PR's what the poster wants? Shrug.  

If you don't like this, just take the one small fix to test/errtest.c
#9441 doesn't in any way contradict what I've said here.

And I don't see how #9452 adds to your argument, but that's okay.  You disagree with what I'm doing here, and that's okay.  You're a committer, I'm not, and I'm okay with that.  Doesn't mean that I'm wrong. :)

Almost every time OpenSSL adds something because "someone might need it," as opposed to doing something that OpenSSL *itself* needs it, the project gets it wrong.  [YAGNI](https://www.martinfowler.com/bliki/Yagni.html), y'all.

issue_context.body:
On hurd we're getting the following error:
```
04-test_err.t ...................... 
# The results of this test will end up in test-runs/test_err
1..1
    # Subtest: ../../test/errtest
    1..4
    ok 1 - preserves_system_error
    ok 2 - vdata_appends
    ok 3 - raised_error
    # ERROR: (string) 'expected == p' failed @ ../test/errtest.c:56
    # --- expected
    # +++ p
    #    0:- ':error::system library:test_print_error_format:Operation not per'
    #    0:+ ':error::system library:test_print_error_format:(os/kern) invalid'
    #                                                        ^^^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^
    #   64:- 'mitted:errtest.c:30:'
    #   64:+ ' address:errtest.c:3'
    #         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    # 
    not ok 4 - test_print_error_format
../../util/wrap.pl ../../test/errtest => 1
not ok 1 - running errtest
```
comments: (POSIX doesn't stipulate specific errno numbers, but rather macros, to get the correct errno, see https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/errno.h.html)

Debian's hurd porterbox seems to be unreachable currently, so I
can test it. I suggest you just make a PR for it.

review_comments: You must *replace* it, not just remove it, since it's a public function.  A macro would work, but lacks the deprecation attribute, so it would be preferable if the functions were properly deprecated, and you left an implementation that just returns zero.
Oh hold on, they're *new* in master...  Never mind then!
I disagree, because it's part of the composition of an error code, so it belongs with the other func/lib/reason defines.
It's part of the composition of *reason codes* (hence `_R_`)
It is also a part of the partitioning of the error-code space, so it should be with the other shifts and masks that define the partitioning.  It's a matter of taste, I guess.
